title: Wayfare Pass Frequent-Rider Refund Relief — Questions Answered
content:
# Frequent-rider refund relief — Wayfare Pass (rider membership)

**What is it?**
When a Wayfare Pass period fee is refunded under the full refund window, the frequent-rider refund relief counts the member's trips charged a fare in the last three months: 3.00 at 20 or more, 1.50 at 10 to 19, nothing below 10.

**What is counted?**
Fare charges on the member's trips in Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares), dated in the last three months, one per trip charged a fare.

**How does it act?**
It lowers the amount withheld from the window refund by that sum. What is withheld never goes below 0.00, so the relief never raises the window refund above the period fee.

**Where are the edges?**

| Trips charged a fare in the last three months | Relief (USD) |
|---|---|
| 20 or more | 3.00 |
| 10 to 19 | 1.50 |
| 0 to 9 | nothing |

20 trips give 3.00 and 19 give 1.50; 10 give 1.50 and 9 give nothing.

**An example?** (hypothetical) With 11.25 withheld and 14 fare charges in the last three months, 9.75 remains withheld.
